802.title: Example of Linear Regression (Supervised Learning)
802.notes: Robot-arm photograph lifting a box has no numerical geometry labels. Problem uses Weight (kg) and Extended Distance (m) as features, torque as floating-point output, linear regression. Kilograms describe mass, and additive regression is not a general m g r law.

806.title: Supervised Learning: Generalization
806.notes: Accurate new data with similar characteristics; separate test set. Literal claim model can always memorize training perfectly is false for restricted model families; counterexample available in preceding affine regression.

807.title: Supervised Learning: Overfitting v/s Underfitting
807.notes: Two-column table defines complexity relative to information, close training particularities and low train/high test versus too simple, high/high. Causes excessive feature/sample ratio, iterations, flexibility versus insufficient features and excessive regularization. Iteration statement needs algorithm/context qualification.

808.title: Supervised Learning: Trade-off
808.notes: Accuracy versus model complexity graph has rising training curve and peaked then declining generalization curve. Sweet spot at generalization peak; underfit left, overfit right. Four design choices feature count, regularization, data size, evaluation strategy. Table low/low desired, verylow/high overfit, high/high underfit. Qualitative, not universal curve law.

809.title: Unsupervised Learning
809.notes: Only input data, no output labels/teacher; identify patterns, regularities, structure. Lack of known correct outputs complicates usefulness evaluation; manual inspection or exploratory analysis often needed.

810.title: Two Major Types of Unsupervised Learning
810.notes: Transformations create representation: dimensionality reduction and feature extraction, PCA/NMF; clustering partitions similar samples, K-Means and Density-Based Spatial Clustering listed. No derivation of PCA/NMF/DBSCAN is supplied.

811.title: Clustering: K-Means
811.notes: Flow: dataset X, initialize k random centers, nearest assignment, update arithmetic means, iterate red arrows, stop unchanged and return k clusters. Screenshot exact import mglearn; mglearn.plots.plot_kmeans_algorithm(). Three colored clusters, triangles centers: blue 0 upper right, red 1 bottom, green 2 left. Recompute Centers (3) is panel label, not number of update passes guaranteed. Flow simplified; empty clusters/ties/tolerance not addressed.

812.title: Zone Clustering: K-Means
812.notes: Unknown indoor robot records temperature °C and Wi-Fi %, no labeled targets; choose three zones from readings. Feature-space groups do not prove spatial connectivity or room identity.

813.title: Zone Clustering: K-Means (Code)
813.notes: Imports numpy, pyplot, sklearn.cluster.KMeans; np.random.seed(42). zone_A=np.random.normal([10,20],[2,5],(100,2)); B means [22,90], C [25,40], same scales and shape. Each row has temp/Wi-Fi, 100 per zone. ±2/±5 mean standard deviations, not hard bounds; normal Wi-Fi model can exceed 100%.

816.title: Unsupervised Learning: Robotics Examples
816.notes: Table four pairings: clustering terrain types raw LiDAR; anomaly detection abnormal joint torque due mechanical failure; dimension reduction compact LiDAR for real-time; image compression similar pixel colors/fewer bits. No guarantee anomalies uniquely diagnose mechanical failure.

817.title: Reinforcement Learning
817.notes: Trial/error agent environment interaction; critic rewards/penalties; maximize cumulative reward. Agent learner/decision maker, environment outside agent, state current representation, action incorrectly defined as set of possible moves (action space). Only after a sequence overstates reward timing; environment need not be physical. These qualifications require explicit conflict binding when tested.

818.title: Reinforcement Learning
818.notes: Loop observes STATE, takes ACTION, environment REWARD, updates brain, repeats; cartoon shows same clockwise sequence. Challenges credit assignment and exploration/exploitation. Named algorithms Q-Learning, Sarsa, Model-Based Learning; applications autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance. No update equations supplied.

819.title: Summary
819.notes: Recap says ML useful when sensor complexity defeats handcrafted rules; paradigms depend on tasks and available data. Unique warning: complex ML can solve the wrong problem, so retain as examinable problem-framing concept rather than blanket recap exclusion.
